seo.title: Privacy Policy: Data Use and Your Rights | MotelPilot
seo.description: Under this policy, we explain what personal data we collect from visitors, enquirers, owners and guests, how it's used and shared, and your rights.

hero.heading: MotelPilot Privacy Policy
lead: We explain how we handle your personal data and how our responsibilities differ when processing guest information on a property's behalf.

blocks.heading: Who this policy covers
paragraphs: This privacy policy applies to personal data about people who visit our website or get in touch with us, property owners and their representatives, and guests whose data we handle under client agreements. MotelPilot is a Canadian company, and we're responsible for the personal data we collect for our own purposes. Guest data we process on a property's behalf works differently: the property decides how it's used, and we act on its instructions as set out in our agreement.
At least once a year we review this policy, and we update it whenever our practices or legal obligations change.

items.heading: Information you submit
paragraphs: Whatever you enter in our forms, such as your name, email address, phone number, property details and message.

items.heading: Website visits
paragraphs: Technical information, including your IP address, browser, device, the pages you visit and the page that referred you to our site.

items.heading: Client and guest records
paragraphs: Under client agreements, we handle owner contact details, booking records, guest contact information, stay details, guest communications and the operational reports needed to deliver the agreed services. Card payments go only through PCI DSS-compliant processing partners, so card data never passes through our own systems.

blocks.heading: How we use, retain and share data

items.heading: Uses and legal grounds
paragraphs: Personal data lets us answer enquiries, deliver the services we've agreed to, keep in touch with you, see how people use our website and protect our systems. Our legal basis depends on the activity and the law that applies. It can be consent, taking steps toward or performing a contract, a legal obligation, or legitimate interests that don't override your rights. For guest data a client controls, we follow that client's documented instructions.

items.heading: Retention
paragraphs: Data stays with us only as long as its purpose, our agreements and applicable legal requirements call for. We regularly go through what we hold and delete or anonymise anything we no longer need. Client records are returned or deleted as the agreement sets out, unless the law says we must keep them.

items.heading: Sharing
paragraphs: Some data has to go to the providers behind our forms, email and cloud hosting. Where a client agreement calls for it, data also goes to authorised service partners. All of them must have appropriate confidentiality and data protection safeguards in place. We may also disclose data when the law requires it. We never sell personal data.

blocks.heading: Your rights, cookies and data locations

items.heading: Canada
paragraphs: Our handling of personal data follows PIPEDA. Within legal limits, you can ask to see or correct your data, withdraw consent and challenge how we handle it.

items.heading: European Union
paragraphs: For motels and hotels in France, we follow the GDPR. Where it applies, you can ask for access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability, object to processing, withdraw consent and complain to a supervisory authority.

items.heading: Australia
paragraphs: The Australian Privacy Act governs how we handle your information. Subject to its requirements, you can ask to access or correct your personal information and raise a privacy complaint.

items.heading: United States
paragraphs: We comply with the privacy laws of the relevant US states. Depending on your state and whether a given law applies, you may be able to access, correct or delete data, get a copy, appeal a decision or opt out of specified uses. You won't be penalised for using any rights that apply to you.

items.heading: Cookies and choices
paragraphs: The site uses only the cookies it needs to work and runs no analytics cookies. If we add analytics, we'll update this policy first and ask for your consent where it's required. You can block or delete cookies in your browser, though that may affect how the site works.

items.heading: Storage and processing
paragraphs: Your data is hosted on cloud servers in Canada, and French properties can ask for EU storage. Our remote team and service providers may process data in other countries. When required, we put appropriate transfer safeguards in place, including contractual protections. Storing data in the EU doesn't on its own mean all processing happens there.

seo.description: These terms cover use of our website and summarise key service agreement points: USD billing, third-party costs at cost, notice, pauses and plan changes.

hero.heading: MotelPilot Terms and Conditions
lead: Here, we clarify the rules for using our website and explain why your service engagement has its own separate agreement.

blocks.heading: What these terms cover
paragraphs: These terms and conditions apply when you use our website, which gives business owners information about our services while they decide whether to work with us.
Any service engagement is agreed directly with our team and comes with its own client agreement. The service summary below doesn't replace that agreement.

items.heading: Information only
paragraphs: This website is here for general information. It isn't a binding offer to provide services, and visiting it or sending us an enquiry doesn't create a service agreement.

items.heading: Accuracy
paragraphs: We try to keep everything accurate and current, but we can't promise that every page is complete, up to date or error-free. Check details with us before you rely on them for business decisions.

items.heading: Links to other sites
paragraphs: Sometimes we link to third-party websites for convenience. We don't control those sites and aren't responsible for their content, availability or practices. When you visit them, their own terms apply.

items.heading: Acceptable use
paragraphs: Use our website lawfully. Don't try to gain unauthorised access, introduce harmful code, disrupt the site or use it to send fraudulent or abusive material.

blocks.heading: Website content and limits of liability

items.heading: Website liability
paragraphs: As far as the law permits, we aren't liable for losses arising from your use of this website, your inability to access it or your reliance on it, including lost profits, lost data and business interruption. These terms don't exclude any liability that can't lawfully be excluded. Liability for our services is covered in your client agreement.

items.heading: Ownership of content
paragraphs: Unless stated otherwise, the website content, branding and design belong to us or our licensors. Accessing the site doesn't transfer any intellectual property rights to you.

items.heading: Permitted use
paragraphs: You're welcome to view, download and print our content for internal business evaluation, as long as any ownership notices stay intact. To republish, sell or distribute it, you'll need our written permission first, unless the law allows otherwise.

items.heading: Website availability
paragraphs: The website is provided as available. We can't guarantee uninterrupted, secure or error-free access, and we may update, suspend or remove content without notice.

items.heading: Advance billing and payment
items.text: Monthly fees are invoiced in advance at the start of each month, and payment is due within 15 days by ACH, international wire or credit card. Our prices are in USD, though you can pay in CAD, EUR or AUD at the exchange rate on the invoice date. A full management agreement also carries a one-time onboarding fee, separate from the revenue management setup fee.

items.heading: Included and third-party costs
items.text: Your fee pays for our team's time and our own pricing, reporting and BI tools. Third-party costs are billed to your property at cost, with no mark-up from us. These include your PMS, channel manager, other software subscriptions, OTA commissions, photographers and specialist partners.

items.heading: Taxes and transfer charges
items.text: USD prices don't include applicable sales taxes, and we add those only where the law requires it for your property's location. Your bank's transfer charges are yours to pay. Currency-conversion costs for payments in CAD, EUR or AUD are on us.

items.heading: Ending a plan
items.text: Each service's minimum term is set out in its proposal. Once that term is over, you can end your plan with 30 days' written notice, and there's no exit fee. The one-time setup fee can't be refunded after setup work starts, and we don't refund fees already paid for the current month.

items.heading: Pausing a plan
items.text: After the minimum term, you can also pause, again with 30 days' written notice. Monthly billing then stops for up to three months. You won't pay a pause fee, and if you restart within that time, you won't pay a new setup fee either.

items.heading: Changing plans
items.text: Upgrades take effect on the day you make the change, and the price difference is prorated for the rest of that month. Downgrades start from your next billing cycle.

items.heading: Results and refunds
items.text: Revenue results aren't guaranteed, and we don't offer refunds, because market demand, competitors and other outside factors all affect performance. What we do is work closely with you, check results against agreed targets on every monthly strategy call and change the strategy whenever a target is missed.
